questions.q: State what a trace table is used for.

markPoints.concept: to record the value of each variable as a program runs, so a fault can be found
accept: step through|line by line|each step|as it runs|track|follow
markPoints.exemplar: To record the value of each variable as the program runs.

questions.example: To record the value of every variable at each step of a program, so that a fault can be found by seeing where a value first goes wrong.
questions.paraphrase: It tracks what each variable holds line by line while the program executes.
questions.feedback: Variable values, step by step. The point of it is finding where a value first becomes wrong.

questions.q: Complete the trace table for this program, which adds up the numbers 1 to 3.
questions.code:
count = 0
total = 0
while count < 3:
    count = count + 1
    total = total + count
print(total)
questions.feedback: The total is a running sum: 1, then 1 + 2 = 3, then 3 + 3 = 6.
questions.hint: Fill in one row for each time round the loop, after both lines inside it have run.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.1 Lesson 11 — Trace room, station 2: Filling one in

questions.q: Complete the trace table for this program, which counts how many times 20 can be halved.
questions.code:
n = 20
steps = 0
while n > 1:
    n = n // 2
    steps = steps + 1
print(steps)
questions.feedback: Integer division halves and rounds down: 20, 10, 5, 2, 1. Four steps — which is how a binary search behaves on twenty items.
questions.hint: // throws away the remainder, so 5 // 2 is 2, not 2.5.

questions.q: What does this program print for the word shown?
questions.code:
word = 'computer'
out = ''
for i in range(len(word) - 1, -1, -1):
    out = out + word[i]
print(out)
questions.feedback: The loop runs backwards through the string, building it up in reverse.
